description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.name: 7.18.0 Contravariant templates
latest_release.body:
## Features

- **`@template-contravariant`** (also `@psalm-` and `@phpstan-template-contravariant`): a template for a class that only takes values, such as a handler, writer or mapper. A `Sink<Animal>` fits where a `Sink<Dog>` is expected, not the other way round, and Psalm reports the template where the class gives a value out.
  ```php
  /** @template-contravariant T */
  interface Sink {
      /** @param T $value */
      public function put(mixed $value): void;

      /** @return T */
      public function last(): mixed; // InvalidTemplateParam
  }

  /** @param Sink<Dog> $sink */
  function takesDogSink(Sink $sink): void {}

  /** @param Sink<Animal> $animals */
  function f(Sink $animals): void {
      takesDogSink($animals); // no issue
  }
  ```
  Plugins read the variance with `ClassLikeStorage::getTemplateVariance()`. See [Template contravariance](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/7.18.0/docs/annotating_code/templated_annotations.md#template-contravariance); the templated annotations page was rewritten with checked examples. (#14669, @alies-dev)
- **Performance profile**: `--debug-performance` (short name `--profile`) prints where a run spent its time and memory: stages, workers, the slowest files, statements and functions, and plugin handlers. With a path it also writes a JSON profile that you can drop on https://psalm.dev/profile/ to see it as charts; the page reads it in your browser and sends it nowhere.
  ```bash
  vendor/bin/psalm --no-cache --profile=psalm-perf.json
  ```
  See [Finding out why Psalm is slow](https://psalm.dev/docs/running_psalm/performance/). (#14737, #14769, #14807, @alies-dev)
- **Agent skill for Psalm users**: `skills/psalm` teaches AI coding agents to run Psalm, fix its issues, write annotations and edit `psalm.xml` the way the docs recommend. Install it with `npx skills add vimeo/psalm --skill psalm`, with the [`llm/skills`](https://packagist.org/packages/llm/skills) Composer plugin, or by copying `vendor/vimeo/psalm/skills/psalm` into your agent's skills directory. (#13152, @roxblnfk; #14751, @danog; #14795, @roxblnfk)


## Performance

- Lower peak memory while resolving the taint graph. (#14774, @aszenz @orklah)

## Fixes

### Templates and type variables

- `new Pipe(fn (int $x) => ...)` with a `Closure(T): void` constructor param caps `T` at `int`, so a later `$pipe->push('s')` is `IncompatibleTypeParameters` instead of reaching the `int` callback. (#14669, @alies-dev)
- A covariant template in the bound of a method template (`@template U of T`) is reported in a param even after an earlier param used `U` legally. (#14669, @alies-dev)
- Callbacks over a widened type variable (`new Coll([1])`, then `$c->add('x')`) see every value it holds, not only the construction-site ones. (#14551, @shu-chen-dot-ca)
- `null` no longer fits a template without a bound: `fn() => null` for `callable(): T`, `[null]` for `list<T>`. (#14550, @shu-chen-dot-ca)
- Trait method params use the types given to `@use`. (#13429, @jirkace)
- `@implements Wrapper<static>` resolves `static` to the object it is read from, and chained calls on such a value no longer hang. (#14572, @jirkace)
- `@return static<NewK, NewV>` on a template receiver keeps its new type arguments. (#14579, @jirkace)
- An implementation with the same conditional return type as its interface method is not an `ImplementedReturnTypeMismatch`. (#14502, @jirkace)
- A conditional return type reads an argument that does not fit its param as it is (`preg_replace()` on an array of `Stringable` returns an array). (#14421, @jirkace)
- A template array `T` read at a `key-of<T>` offset is `value-of<T>`. (#14586, @jirkace)
- `is_int()`, `is_scalar()` and similar checks narrow a template bounded by `scalar`, `numeric`, `array-key` or an int range instead of reporting `DocblockTypeContradiction`. (#14545, @jirkace)
- A literal class name can be identical to a template `class-string<T>`. (#14365, @jirkace)
- I

Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
